newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rebhold buys Honeyfields, issues cautionary.
newsitem.headline: Rebhold buys Honeyfields, issues cautionary.

text.p: Food, freight and liquour company Rebhold Ltd said on Monday it had acquired Gauteng-based wafers and sugar cones manufacturer and distributor Honeyfields.
In a statement, Rebhold said the deal was subject to the completion of a due diligence investigation it was carrying out.

It said the purchase price would be fixed on a formula which would see Rebhold paying about 4.3 times the average annualised taxed profits achieved by HoneyFields in the 30 months from the effective date of transaction.

"On the assumption the warranted profits for the period are achieved, and depending on if they are exceeded, Rebhold will make the purchase by alloting and issuing between 6.5 million and a maximum of 9.1 million Rebhold shares in three tranches," the statement said.
Rebhold chief executive officer Jacques Kempen said the deal would not have a material effect on earnings or net asset value for the financial year ending June 30.
"Honeyfields fits our profile of well managed businesses that are dominant in their niche markets and that generate cash and substantial profits," Kempen said.
Rebhold's food and distribution operations include Southern Superfoods, Foodpak, Clinecor, M and D Catering and Contract Forwarding.

"It (Honeyfields) also fits into the Southern Superfoods' concept of key brand distribution into the retail and catering markets and complies with our stated objective of expanding our food and distribution interests," Kempen said.
He added there was considerable potential for further expansion in the production and marketing of Honeyfields' products, to the retail industry and for export.
Rebhold also issued another cautionary announcement advising shareholders that it was involved in further negotiations pertaining to other acquisitions which could affect the price of its shares.
